title: Miami Dolphins
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the Miami Dolphins, a professional American football team in the NFL's AFC East division based in the Miami metropolitan area. The document begins with an introduction covering the team's founding by Joe Robbie and Danny Thomas in 1966, its ownership by Stephen M. Ross, home games at Hard Rock Stadium, and its historical achievements, including the NFL's only perfect season (1972), back-to-back Super Bowl victories (VII and VIII), and the Dan Marino era. It then details the franchise's complete history through chronologically organized coaching tenures, from Don Shula's dominant years (1970–1995) through subsequent coaches including Jimmy Johnson, Dave Wannstedt, Nick Saban, Cam Cameron, Tony Sparano, Joe Philbin, Adam Gase, Brian Flores, Mike McDaniel, and Jeff Hafley. The document covers the team's rivalries, including divisional matchups with the New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and New York Jets, as well as conference and historic rivalries with the Jacksonville Jaguars, Indianapolis Colts, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Kansas City Chiefs, and others. Additional sections describe the team's facilities (the Orange Bowl and Hard Rock Stadium, plus training complexes), franchise branding elements such as the evolution of logos and uniforms (from the original leaping dolphin to the current stylized swimming dolphin), throwback and special uniforms, the fight song, cheerleaders, volunteer programs, and mascots (T.D., Dolfan Denny, and Flipper). The document also addresses radio and television broadcasting arrangements, franchise information including Pro Football Hall of Fame inductees, retired numbers (Bob Griese's #12, Dan Marino's #13, and Larry Csonka's #39), individual award winners, Pro Bowl selections, the franchise's 50 greatest players, the Ring of Honor/Honor Roll, the Joe Robbie Alumni Plaza Walk of Fame, first-round draft picks, and the team's coaching staff and front office structure.
